question: What does the literature say about YK11’s mechanism of action, androgen-receptor selectivity, and myostatin inhibition?

compound.name: YK11 (YK-11 / myostine)
compound.class: steroidal AR partial agonist / gene-selective SARM candidate; marketed as myostatin inhibitor

claims.statement: YK11 is a partial agonist of the androgen receptor (ARE-luciferase; nuclear translocation).

supporting.notes: Kanno 2011: ARE-luciferase max ~10–20% of DHT; nuclear translocation of AR.

claims.funding_notes: Academic Japanese lab (Toho/Kanno); single-lab discovery package.

claims.statement: YK11 does not induce AR N/C interaction and can prevent DHT-mediated N/C interaction.

supporting.notes: Mammalian two-hybrid: YK11 null like hydroxyflutamide; co-treatment reduces DHT N/C signal.

claims.funding_notes: Same lab; limited independent multi-lab replication of N/C package in acquisition set.

claims.statement: YK11 is a gene-selective AR agonist (differential gene program vs DHT in AR-positive cells).

supporting.notes: MDA-MB-453 endogenous genes: FKBP51/FGF18 ≈ DHT; SARG DHT-only; HSD11B2 weaker with YK11.

claims.funding_notes: Gene selectivity ≠ tissue selectivity; cancer cell line context.

claims.statement: YK11 is a clinically meaningful tissue-selective SARM (muscle/bone ≫ prostate/androgenic tissues).

supporting.notes: Authors proposed SARM from gene selectivity + partial agonism; no Hershberger A/A package in set.
C2C12 myogenic markers support anabolic-leaning cell activity only.

contradicting.notes: Park 2022 notes mechanisms incompletely understood and no human trials.

claims.funding_notes: Tissue selectivity Speculative/Unknown; steroidal scaffold; marketing overclaims.

claims.statement: YK11 induces myogenic differentiation markers in C2C12 (MyHC, MyoD, Myf5, myogenin) in an AR-dependent manner.

supporting.notes: Kanno 2013 full text: MyHC and MRFs; FLU attenuates; n=3; Student's t-test.

claims.funding_notes: MEXT / Open Research Center; mouse cell line only.

claims.statement: YK11 induces follistatin (Fst) mRNA in C2C12 via AR; DHT does not under the same conditions; Fst is required for YK11-driven Myf5 upregulation.

supporting.notes: Fst mRNA Day 2/4; FLU and AR siRNA blunt Fst; neutralizing anti-Fst Ab abolishes Myf5 induction.

claims.funding_notes: Core of indirect myostatin-pathway narrative; single-lab C2C12.

claims.statement: YK11 is a direct myostatin (MSTN) ligand antagonist or ActRIIB receptor antagonist.

contradicting.notes: Primary pathway is AR → Fst; no MSTN binding or ActRIIB competition assay in pivotal paper.

claims.funding_notes: Literature does not support direct MSTN pharmacology; claim effectively unsupported.

claims.statement: YK11 functions as a 'myostatin inhibitor' via indirect Fst-mediated antagonism of TGF-β family ligands including myostatin (cells).

supporting.notes: Fst induction + Ab rescue supports functional Fst arm for Myf5; Fst is known MSTN/activin antagonist.
Park 2022 secondary: blocks myostatin by upregulating follistatin via AR.

contradicting.notes: Lee 2021 title hardens soft mechanism into categorical inhibitor; abstract-level sepsis model; not human pathway proof.

claims.funding_notes: Human systemic myostatin blockade: Speculative/Unknown. Marketing primary-identity label exceeds data.

claims.statement: YK11 has proven anabolic efficacy and safe oral doses in humans (e.g., community 5–15 mg/day).

contradicting.notes: Regulators: unauthorized; not reviewed for safety/efficacy/quality.

claims.funding_notes: No RCTs, PK/PD, or dose-finding. Community doses not evidence.

claims.statement: YK11 upregulates osteoblastic proliferation/differentiation markers via AR (MC3T3-E1).

supporting.notes: Yatsu 2018: proliferation, mineralization, OPG/OCN; AR antagonist attenuates; p-Akt.
Wang 2025 BMSC + rat cranial defect abstract-level extension.

claims.funding_notes: Same-lab osteoblast paper + later independent phenotype; clinical bone benefit Unknown.

claims.statement: YK11 attenuates sepsis-related muscle wasting/mortality in mice via myostatin-pathway effects.

supporting.notes: Lee 2021 abstract: pathway markers, cytokines, organ injury, mortality; full methods not retrieved.

claims.funding_notes: NRF Korea; no COI declared. Disease model ≠ bodybuilding anabolism.

claims.statement: YK11 shows organ toxicity / adverse organ and CNS signals in rodents at experimental exposures.

supporting.notes: Dahleh line: hippocampus oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, memory; organ-focused work ± exercise.

claims.funding_notes: Declared no COI on 2024 CBI paper; human organ safety Unknown.

claims.statement: YK11-containing products are unauthorized SARMs with serious class health-risk warnings; WADA-prohibited.

supporting.notes: Health Canada unauthorized SARM advisories naming myostine/YK-11 class products.
WADA Prohibited List — SARMs including YK-11.

claims.funding_notes: Regulatory fact; specific pure-YK11 human event rates remain Unknown.

claims.statement: Stacking YK11 with full AR agonists may impair full-agonist N/C-dependent signaling.

supporting.notes: Kanno 2011: prevents DHT N/C; can repress DHT-driven ARE-luciferase at high concentration.
Park 2022 flags stacking risk from N/C interference.

claims.funding_notes: Mechanistically grounded in vitro; clinical stack antagonism Speculative.

recommendations.statement: Describe YK11 as a steroidal gene-selective AR partial agonist with AR-dependent follistatin induction in C2C12 — not as a primary direct myostatin inhibitor.
recommendations.inference_note: Correct MoA language per Kanno 2011/2013; marketing direct-MSTN framing exceeds data.

recommendations.statement: Recommend against marketing/community claims that YK11 is a proven or direct myostatin inhibitor / clinical myostatin pathway drug.
recommendations.inference_note: Established that literature does not support direct MSTN blockade or human pathway proof; overclaim relative to data.

recommendations.statement: Recommend against claims that gene-selective partial agonism proves safer, prostate-sparing tissue-selective SARM status in humans.
recommendations.inference_note: Gene selectivity Probable in vitro; tissue selectivity Speculative/Unknown; no Hershberger package.

recommendations.statement: Do not recommend any human dose, cycle length, or stacking protocol for muscle gain — community 5–15 mg/day is Unknown PK and outcome evidence.
recommendations.inference_note: Unknown = no dose recommendation (DR rule). Zero human PK/efficacy trials.

recommendations.statement: Do not initiate YK11 for performance or medical anabolism on current evidence; prefer agents with human data when medical anabolism is indicated.
recommendations.inference_note: Human benefit Unknown; regulatory/class safety concerns Probable–Established; unauthorized product.

recommendations.statement: Athletes subject to WADA: do not use YK11 (prohibited SARM).

If research-chemical exposure occurs despite lack of efficacy evidence: baseline and on-drug bloodwork (CMP/LFTs, lipids, CBC, T/LH/FSH, estradiol; PSA by age/risk) and BP; stop for jaundice, severe lipid collapse, hypertension crisis, mood crisis, or hypogonadal crisis.
recommendations.inference_note: Class SARM/AAS harm-reduction prudence; not evidence YK11 is manageable-safe.

recommendations.statement: Expect possible HPG suppression as with other AR agonists; do not assume 'SARM = no PCT needed'; no evidence-based YK11-specific PCT protocol exists — do not invent PCT doses; seek medical evaluation for persistent hypogonadism.
recommendations.inference_note: Class-level suppression Probable; YK11-specific magnitude Unknown; PCT efficacy after YK11 Unknown.

recommendations.statement: Against complex stacks with other SARMs/AAS for optimization: additive class risks plus theoretical N/C interference blunting full agonists.
recommendations.inference_note: Mechanistic N/C interference Probable in vitro; clinical stack antagonism Speculative.

recommendations.statement: Treat grey-market products as high risk for mislabeling, adulteration, and wrong dose; not pharmaceutical-grade.
recommendations.inference_note: JAMA and regulatory product-testing patterns for 'SARM' market.

recommendations.statement: Recommend against use in pregnancy, adolescence, tested sport, active liver disease, uncontrolled CVD, prostate cancer history, or near-term fertility goals without medical supervision.
recommendations.inference_note: Class harm inference; sport ban Established for athletes.

recommendations.statement: No timing recommendation relative to training, meals, or circadian rhythm.
recommendations.inference_note: No human PK or timing trials.

bro_science_claims.claim: YK11 is a direct / proven myostatin inhibitor (MSTN ligand or receptor blocker).
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Kanno 2013 pathway is AR-dependent Fst induction; no direct MSTN binding data. Lee 2021 title language is framing compression, not ligand proof.

bro_science_claims.claim: Gene-selective SARM = safer than steroids / no sides / prostate-safe.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Gene selectivity is in vitro only; tissue selectivity unproven. Health Canada class CV/liver warnings and rodent CNS/organ signals contradict 'no sides'.

bro_science_claims.claim: Anabolic in humans at 5–15 mg/day oral (standard gym dose).
bro_science_claims.literature_note: No peer-reviewed human dose-finding, PK, or body-composition RCTs. Community tradition only.

bro_science_claims.claim: 4–8 week cycles with no liver toxicity under ~30 mg.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Absolute safety thresholds invented; no human LFT RCT for YK11.

bro_science_claims.claim: Stacks well with other SARMs/AAS for synergy.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Clinical stack benefit Speculative. Mechanistic N/C interference may impair full-agonist signaling (Kanno 2011; Park 2022) — Probable in vitro; additive class toxicity risks unquantified.

bro_science_claims.claim: YK11 is a partial AR agonist / gene-selective SARM candidate with unique Fst arm vs DHT in C2C12.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Supported by Kanno 2011/2013 in vitro; human translation and clinical SARM tissue package remain open.

bro_science_claims.claim: Clinical myostatin-blocker / cachexia drug equivalent to biologics.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: No approval, no pivotal human trials; different mechanism class from mAbs/ActRII traps.

bro_science_claims.claim: SARM = no PCT needed after YK11.
bro_science_claims.literature_note: AR agonists suppress HPG by class; no YK11 endocrine recovery trials. 'No PCT' is unsupported.
